prompt: I have this Rust code for a TCP connection handler that uses a big match statement to handle different states. It's getting unwieldy — every time I add a new state I have to touch 4 different match arms scattered across the file. Can you refactor it to be more maintainable?

assertions.name: eliminates_string_state
assertions.description: Replaces string-based state ('disconnected', etc.) with typed states (enum variants or separate structs)

assertions.name: explains_pattern_choice
assertions.description: Explains WHY the chosen pattern (State vs enum FSM) is appropriate for this specific case, with tradeoffs

assertions.name: compiles_or_near_compiles
assertions.description: The refactored code is syntactically valid Rust that would compile (or nearly compile) — not pseudocode

assertions.name: handles_all_original_states
assertions.description: All 4 states (disconnected, connecting, connected, error) and their events are preserved in the refactored code
